name: Travel & Airlines
tagline: Bookings, passengers, ticket revenue and fares, on-time performance, delays, cancellations and load factor for airlines and travel agencies
description: Flight booking and PNR exports from airline reservation systems and GDS (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport Galileo, Navitaire), air ticket sales registers from travel agencies and OTAs (MakeMyTrip, Cleartrip, Yatra, EaseMyTrip, Riya, Expedia TAAP) and corporate travel tools (SAP Concur, Navan), flight-operations data with on-time performance, delays and cancellations such as the US BTS On-Time Performance tables, route traffic and load factor reports (BTS T-100, DGCA monthly traffic data) and passenger satisfaction surveys.

fields.label: Booking / PNR
fields.description: Identifies each booking; a PNR with several passengers or flights may repeat on several rows.

fields.label: Flight distance
fields.description: Distance flown per flight, in kilometres or miles; ASK, RPK and stage length follow its unit.

fields.label: Fare / ticket amount
fields.description: What the passenger paid for the ticket, including taxes and fees unless only a base fare is given.

fields.label: Arrival delay (minutes)
fields.description: Minutes after the scheduled arrival; early arrivals are negative where the data records them.

fields.label: Service rating (any aspect)
fields.description: One of a survey's service scores; only one is mapped, the rest stay as columns.

subDomains.name: Flight bookings & tickets
subDomains.description: One row per booking, PNR or ticket with booking and travel dates, airline, route, cabin, passengers and fare, as in airline reservation exports and travel-agency ticket sales registers.

subDomains.name: Flight operations & on-time performance
subDomains.description: One row per flight with scheduled date, airline, flight number, route, departure and arrival delays, cancellation and diversion, as in BTS on-time data or an airline's flight log.

subDomains.name: Route traffic & load factor
subDomains.description: One row per route, airline or flight per period with seats offered, passengers carried, departures and distance, as in BTS T-100 segment data or DGCA traffic reports.

subDomains.name: Passenger satisfaction survey
subDomains.description: One row per surveyed passenger with travel class, trip type, flight distance, delays, service ratings and an overall satisfied or dissatisfied answer.

kpis.name: Passengers (all bookings)
kpis.definition: Passengers on every booking, before removing cancelled bookings.

variants.label: Distinct ticket numbers
variants.caveat: No passenger count, so each distinct ticket is one passenger.

kpis.name: Ticket revenue (all bookings)
kpis.definition: Fares on every booking, before removing cancelled bookings.

variants.label: Base fare + taxes
variants.caveat: No total fare column, so fares are the base fare plus taxes and fees.

variants.label: Base fare
variants.caveat: Only a base fare is available, so taxes and fees are left out.

kpis.name: Delay minutes by cause (all causes)
kpis.definition: Arrival delay minutes attributed to the five standard causes: carrier, weather, air traffic system, security and late-arriving aircraft.
kpis.formula: Σ carrier + weather + NAS + security + late aircraft delay minutes

kpis.name: Bookings
kpis.definition: Number of distinct bookings (PNRs) made, including any later cancelled.

variants.label: Row count (no booking ID)
variants.caveat: No booking ID column, so every row is counted as one booking. Check the grain.

kpis.name: Passengers
kpis.definition: Passengers booked or carried, excluding cancelled and refunded bookings.

variants.label: All rows
variants.caveat: No booking status, so passengers are taken as recorded.

kpis.name: Ticket revenue
kpis.definition: Fares on bookings that were not cancelled or refunded.
kpis.formula: Σ fare, excluding cancelled and refunded bookings

variants.label: All bookings
variants.caveat: No booking status, so revenue is taken as recorded; any cancelled or refunded tickets are included.

pitfalls: A sales register books revenue on the issue date, while airlines recognise it when the flight is flown; analyse by the date that matches the report you compare with.

kpis.name: Average fare
kpis.definition: Ticket revenue per passenger, on bookings that were not cancelled.

variants.label: Ticket revenue ÷ net bookings
variants.caveat: No passenger count, so this is the average fare per booking, not per passenger.

variants.label: Ticket revenue ÷ bookings
variants.caveat: No passenger count or status, so this is revenue per booking, including any cancelled ones.

pitfalls: Average fare moves with the mix of routes, cabins and how early people book; compare it within one route and cabin.

kpis.name: Booking cancellation rate
kpis.definition: Share of bookings that were cancelled or refunded.
pitfalls: Bookings for future flights can still cancel, so the latest booking months understate the final rate.

kpis.name: Average booking lead time
kpis.definition: Average days between booking and departure.
kpis.formula: Average of (travel date − booking date) in days

variants.label: Days-before-departure column
variants.caveat: Uses the days-before-departure column as reported.

kpis.name: Passenger survey responses
kpis.definition: Number of passenger survey responses.

kpis.name: Passenger satisfaction rate
kpis.definition: Share of surveyed passengers who said they were satisfied.
pitfalls: Check which answers count as satisfied in Check & map › Value meanings; a 'neutral' answer is not satisfied.

kpis.name: Average overall rating
kpis.definition: Average overall rating passengers gave.
pitfalls: Check the scale (out of 5 or 10) before comparing airlines or surveys.

kpis.name: Flights scheduled
kpis.definition: Flights scheduled to operate, including any later cancelled.
kpis.formula: Σ departures scheduled (or one per flight row)

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: Every row is counted as one scheduled flight.

kpis.name: Passenger load factor
kpis.definition: Share of seat capacity filled with passengers, weighted by distance when it is known.

variants.label: Passengers ÷ seats
variants.caveat: Passengers ÷ seats, not weighted by distance.

benchmark.note: IATA's global passenger load factor has run at about 80–85% in recent years; low-cost carriers on busy domestic routes often run higher.

pitfalls: A load factor is a ratio of totals: recompute it from passengers and seats (or RPK and ASK), never average flight-level percentages.

kpis.name: On-time performance
kpis.definition: Share of flights with a recorded arrival that arrived less than 15 minutes after schedule.
kpis.formula: Flights arriving under 15 minutes late ÷ flights with an arrival delay

variants.label: Not flagged as delayed 15+ minutes
variants.caveat: Uses the 15-minute delay flag as recorded.

variants.label: On-time flag
variants.caveat: Uses the on-time flag as recorded; its threshold may not be 15 minutes.

variants.label: On time ÷ on time or delayed
variants.caveat: Uses the flight status: flights marked on time ÷ flights marked on time or delayed.

variants.label: Departure delay under 15 minutes
variants.caveat: No arrival delay, so this is departure punctuality (within 15 minutes of schedule).

benchmark.note: Indicative arrival on-time performance (within 15 minutes) for large airlines; season, weather and hub congestion move it by several points.

pitfalls: Cancelled and diverted flights have no arrival delay, so they drop out of this rate; read it next to the cancellation rate.
Some airlines and regulators publish departure punctuality rather than arrival; compare on the same basis.

kpis.name: Average arrival delay
kpis.definition: Average minutes between scheduled and actual arrival over flights with a recorded arrival; early arrivals count as negative minutes where the data records them.
kpis.formula: Average of arrival delay in minutes
pitfalls: Some files floor early arrivals at zero (BTS ARR_DELAY_NEW) and some keep them negative; the two give different averages.

kpis.name: Flight cancellation rate
kpis.definition: Share of scheduled flights that were cancelled.

variants.label: (Scheduled − performed) ÷ scheduled
variants.caveat: Departures scheduled but not performed, as a share of scheduled; extra unscheduled flights lower it.

kpis.name: Average departure delay
kpis.definition: Average minutes between scheduled and actual departure over flights that departed.
kpis.formula: Average of departure delay in minutes

kpis.name: Seats offered
kpis.definition: Seats offered for sale on the flights or routes in the period.

kpis.name: Available seat kilometres
kpis.definition: Capacity offered: seats × distance flown. Kilometres give ASK; a distance in miles gives ASM.
kpis.formula: Σ seats × distance (or the ASK column)

variants.label: Seats × distance
variants.caveat: Seats × distance; the unit follows the distance column (miles give ASM).

kpis.name: Revenue passenger kilometres
kpis.definition: Traffic carried: paying passengers × distance flown. Kilometres give RPK; a distance in miles gives RPM.
kpis.formula: Σ passengers × distance (or the RPK column)

variants.label: Passengers × distance
variants.caveat: Passengers × distance; the unit follows the distance column (miles give RPM).

kpis.name: Flights operated
kpis.definition: Flights that actually operated, excluding cancellations.
kpis.formula: Σ departures performed (or flights not cancelled)

variants.label: Flights without a cancelled status
variants.caveat: Flights whose status is not cancelled, including any with a blank status.

kpis.name: Diversion rate
kpis.definition: Share of scheduled flights that landed somewhere other than the planned destination.

kpis.name: Delayed flights
kpis.definition: Flights that arrived 15 minutes or more after schedule.
kpis.formula: Count of flights with arrival delay ≥ 15 minutes

variants.label: Delayed 15+ flag
variants.caveat: Uses the 15-minute delay flag as recorded.

variants.label: Delayed status
variants.caveat: Uses the flight status; its delay threshold may not be 15 minutes.

kpis.name: Average delay of late flights
kpis.definition: Average arrival delay of the flights that arrived 15 minutes or more late.
kpis.formula: Average arrival delay where arrival delay ≥ 15 minutes

variants.label: Average delay of flights 15+ minutes late

kpis.name: Arrival delay minutes
kpis.definition: Total minutes flights arrived late, counting late flights only.
kpis.formula: Σ arrival delay where arrival delay > 0

kpis.name: Airline-caused delay share
kpis.definition: Share of attributed delay minutes caused by the airline itself (crew, maintenance, cleaning, fuelling).
kpis.formula: Carrier delay minutes ÷ delay minutes of all five causes

kpis.name: Reactionary delay share
kpis.definition: Share of attributed delay minutes caused by the aircraft arriving late from its previous flight.
kpis.formula: Late aircraft delay minutes ÷ delay minutes of all five causes

kpis.name: Average taxi-out time
kpis.definition: Average minutes from leaving the gate to take-off.

kpis.name: Passengers per flight
kpis.definition: Passengers carried per flight operated.

kpis.name: Average stage length
kpis.definition: Average distance per flight, in the unit of the distance column.
kpis.formula: Σ distance × departures ÷ departures (or average distance per row)

variants.label: Average distance
variants.caveat: Average of the distance column, one value per row.

kpis.name: Commission and markup earned
kpis.definition: Commission, markup and service fees earned on bookings that were not cancelled.

variants.label: All bookings
variants.caveat: No booking status, so commission on cancelled bookings is included.

kpis.name: Agency commission %
kpis.definition: Commission and markup earned as a share of ticket revenue.

kpis.name: Refunds
kpis.definition: Amounts refunded to passengers.

kpis.name: Passenger no-show rate
kpis.definition: Share of bookings not cancelled whose passengers did not turn up for the flight.

kpis.name: Premium cabin share
kpis.definition: Share of passengers travelling in business or first class.
pitfalls: Premium economy is counted apart, not as premium; check the classes in Check & map › Value meanings.

kpis.name: Passengers per booking
kpis.definition: Passengers per booking, before removing cancellations.

kpis.name: Unique travellers
kpis.definition: Distinct passengers or travellers who booked in the period.

kpis.name: Routes served
kpis.definition: Distinct routes (sectors) in the period.

kpis.name: Cancelled flights
kpis.definition: Scheduled flights that were cancelled.

kpis.name: Carrier delay minutes
kpis.definition: Arrival delay minutes the airline caused (crew, maintenance, cleaning, fuelling, baggage).

kpis.name: Weather delay minutes
kpis.definition: Arrival delay minutes caused by significant weather.

kpis.name: Air traffic delay minutes
kpis.definition: Arrival delay minutes caused by the air traffic system: congestion, air traffic control and non-extreme weather.

kpis.name: Security delay minutes
kpis.definition: Arrival delay minutes caused by security events or long screening queues.

kpis.name: Late aircraft delay minutes
kpis.definition: Arrival delay minutes caused by the aircraft arriving late from its previous flight.

charts.title: Ticket revenue by travel month
charts.reason: One revenue measure over continuous time, bucketed by travel date so revenue sits with the flight; the soft fill shows volume without hiding the season.

charts.title: Average fare over time
charts.reason: Average fare is a ratio, so it is recomputed per period (revenue ÷ passengers) and drawn as a line, never summed.

charts.title: Bookings by booking date
charts.reason: Bookings made per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: On-time performance over time
charts.reason: OTP is a ratio, recomputed per period from flights on time and flights arrived, and drawn as a line.

charts.title: Flights scheduled over time
charts.reason: Flights per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Delay minutes by cause
charts.reason: Five causes that add up to the attributed delay each month: stacked columns show both the total and which causes grew.

charts.title: Passengers over time
charts.reason: One traffic measure over continuous time: the soft fill shows volume and seasonality.

charts.title: Load factor over time
charts.reason: Load factor is a ratio, recomputed per period from passengers and seats and drawn as a line, never averaged.

charts.title: Ticket revenue by airline
charts.reason: One measure across named airlines: sorted horizontal bars keep the names readable. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Passengers by cabin
charts.reason: A few cabins as parts of all passengers: a donut shows the economy-to-premium mix at a glance.

charts.title: Top routes by passengers
charts.reason: One measure across many named routes: sorted bars of the top 12 show where the traffic is.

charts.title: Top destinations by passengers
charts.reason: One measure across many destinations: sorted horizontal bars of the top 12.

charts.title: Ticket revenue by channel
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few booking channels: a donut shows the direct-versus-agent mix.

charts.title: On-time performance by airline
charts.reason: A rate compared across airlines: sorted bars of the recomputed OTP, with airlines under 30 flights hidden as too small.

charts.title: Average arrival delay by origin airport
charts.reason: An average compared across airports: sorted bars show where delays start, with airports under 30 flights hidden.

charts.title: Passengers by airline
charts.reason: One measure across named airlines: sorted bars show market share by passengers. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Load factor by airline
charts.reason: A ratio compared across airlines: sorted bars of the recomputed load factor, never an average of percentages.

charts.title: Satisfaction rate by cabin
charts.reason: A rate compared across a few cabins: sorted bars of the recomputed satisfaction rate.

charts.title: Satisfaction rate by trip type
charts.reason: Business and leisure travellers judge differently: columns of the recomputed rate per trip type.

charts.title: Satisfaction rate by passenger type
charts.reason: Loyal and first-time passengers compared on one recomputed rate.

charts.title: Average fare by days booked ahead
charts.reason: Do early bookers pay less? The recomputed average fare per lead-time band, in band order.

charts.title: How far ahead passengers book
charts.reason: The spread of booking lead times: a histogram of bookings per band shows the booking window.

charts.title: Booking cancellation rate by airline
charts.reason: A rate compared across airlines: sorted bars of the recomputed rate, with airlines under 30 bookings hidden as too small.

charts.title: Average fare by number of stops
charts.reason: A few stop counts and one recomputed average: columns show what a non-stop flight costs extra.

charts.title: On-time performance by weekday
charts.reason: Seven ordered weekdays and one recomputed rate: columns show which days run late.

charts.title: How late flights arrive
charts.reason: The spread of arrival delays: a histogram shows the long tail of very late flights that an average hides.

charts.title: Why flights are cancelled
charts.reason: A handful of causes (carrier, weather, air traffic, security) as parts of all cancellations: a donut shows the split.

charts.title: Flight cancellation rate by airline
charts.reason: A rate compared across airlines: sorted bars of the recomputed rate, with airlines under 30 flights hidden.

charts.title: Load factor by route
charts.reason: Which routes fly full and which fly empty: sorted bars of the recomputed load factor per route.

charts.title: Seats offered vs load factor by airline
charts.reason: Two measures per airline: a scatter shows who adds capacity without filling it, with no misleading dual axis.

charts.title: Satisfaction rate by arrival delay
charts.reason: Does a late arrival cost satisfaction? The recomputed rate per delay band, in band order.

charts.title: Satisfaction rate by flight distance
charts.reason: Short hops and long hauls compared on one recomputed rate, band by band.

charts.title: Airline scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per airline, read side by side: a sortable table compares bookings, passengers, revenue and fare.

charts.title: Airline punctuality scorecard
charts.reason: Flights, OTP, average delay and cancellations per airline in one sortable table.

charts.title: Origin airport scorecard
charts.reason: Flights, OTP, departure delay and cancellations per origin airport in one sortable table.

charts.title: Route scorecard
charts.reason: Passengers, seats and load factor per route in one sortable table.

pitfalls: On-time performance, load factor and average fare are ratios of totals: recompute them per period and group, never average flight- or route-level percentages.
Cancelled and diverted flights have no arrival delay, so they fall out of delay averages and on-time performance; read those next to the cancellation rate.
A booking (PNR) can hold several passengers and several flights: count passengers and tickets, not rows, when the file has one row per PNR or per flight coupon.
A sales register books revenue on the issue date, while airlines recognise it when the flight is flown; analyse by the date that matches the report you compare with.
ASK, RPK and stage length follow the unit of the distance column: kilometres give ASK and RPK, miles give ASM and RPM.
Refunds, voids and reissues often appear as extra rows with negative or repeated amounts; check the status values before summing fares.
